title: Tropical Spanning Criteria, Exact F2-Polynomial No-Strings Certificates, and Machine-Checked Energy-Barrier Bounds for 3D Translation-Invariant Stabilizer Codes
abstract: Certifying that a three-dimensional translation-invariant CSS or trivariate bicycle (TB) stabilizer code is a genuine Type-II fracton phase—free of mobile string-like logical operators along every lattice direction v in Z^3 \ {0} and of every period p >= 1—is the algebraic gatekeeper for logarithmic energy barriers and partial self-correction. Recent universal certification frameworks (e.g., Xu & Xu, arXiv:2611.06469) and formal QEC verification libraries (QECert, arXiv:2611.05047) highlight a persistent gap: directional tests restricted to coordinate axes or short lattice vectors can be fooled by higher-slope stealth strings, while floating-point or heuristic solvers leave formal soundness gaps. We close this gap with three tightly integrated contributions. First, we prove the Tropical Spanning Criterion (Theorem 2.3): because every element of F_2bar^* is a root of unity, a nontrivial coprime 2-generator 3D translation-invariant CSS code (f, g) in F_2[x^{+-1}, y^{+-1}, z^{+-1}]^2 (gcd(f, g) = 1, <f, g> != R) satisfies the Universal All-Direction No-Strings Condition if and only if every geometrically irreducible curve component C_i of V(f, g) in (F_2bar^*)^3 has a full-rank tropical valuation fan, rank_Q(Trop(C_i)) = 3. Second, we introduce a zero-floating-point-trust certificate format (FRACTON-CERT-1.0) combining exact F_2[x,y,z] resultant Bezout cofactors, six F_2[t] axis-content Bezout witnesses, exact F_4(t) birational parameterizations with explicit rational inverses t = N(x,y)/D(x,y) (Proposition 3.1, blocking reducible-factor forgeries by reduced-degree matching), exact component completeness prod_i H_i(x,y) = R_z(x,y), and exact place-valuation ray matrices with det(W) != 0, alongside dual coprime F_2[x,y,z]/F_4-point obstruction certificates for string-harboring codes. Third, we mechanize 16 core algebraic, tropical, and conditional scale-ladder energy-barrier theorems culminating in B(d) >= c_1 floor(log_{2*beta+3}(d/R_0)) (Theorem 4.1) in zero-dependency Lean 4 (v4.35.0, 0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice). Across a systematic scan of 155 weight-4 and weight-5 3D TB codes (strictly separating 1 non-coprime code and 10 trivial product-state codes with <f,g> = R, leaving 144 nontrivial codes), 24/103 (23.3%) of nontrivial codes passing all coordinate-axis checks—and 23/102 (22.5%) passing all 13 unit-box directions (||v||_inf = 1)—harbor ||v||_inf = 2 stealth rigid strings such as v = (0,-1,2) and v = (-2,-1,2), collapsing their energy barriers to E_string <= 6 despite fracton-like finite-torus homology k(L); extending the screen to ||v||_inf = 3 exposes 12 additional traps, raising nontrivial false-positive rates to 35.0% (axis-only) and 34.3% (unit-box). All 8 published atlas certificates verify with zero floating-point operations and reject 26/26 live adversarial forgery and type-injection attacks.
